name: MTS Rising College Scholarship
summary: A $2,500 scholarship for high school seniors who have been accepted into a marine studies program at a 2- or 4-year college. It is the only Marine Technology Society award open to high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Join MTS as a student member, then apply online with an essay of up to 500 words, a list of marine activities and honors, a list of relevant courses, one recommendation letter and an unofficial transcript. The 2026 round has closed, and MTS says 2027 details will be posted in January.
amount_text: $2,500 one-time
deadline_text: The 2026 round is closed. Details for 2027 are expected in January 2027.
other_requirements: You must be an active MTS member (student membership is $25 a year) and be accepted into a 2- or 4-year marine studies program.

name: AMS First-Year Undergraduate Scholarship
summary: A $5,000 scholarship, paid over the first two years of college, for high school seniors who plan to major in atmospheric, oceanic or hydrologic science. Ocean science majors qualify. Marine biology does not.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the application form, an unofficial transcript covering the last three years of high school and one recommendation letter. The deadline is usually in early February of senior year.
amount_text: $5,000 total ($2,500 a year for freshman and sophomore years)
deadline_text: Early February of senior year. The deadline for fall 2026 entry was February 6, 2026.
other_requirements: You must plan a degree in atmospheric science or a related ocean or water science. Marine biology does not count. You must enter college full-time in the fall after senior year. The second year's payment requires finishing freshman year successfully.

name: The Science Ambassador Scholarship
summary: Five $20,000 scholarships for women and non-binary students who will major in a STEM field. High school seniors and current undergraduates can apply.
how_to_apply: Film a video of up to 3 minutes teaching a STEM topic you love, post it publicly on YouTube in widescreen format (not as a Short), and submit the online application by December 14, 2026.
amount_text: $20,000 one-time, paid to your college
deadline_text: December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM Central Time
other_requirements: Open to women and non-binary students. STEM must be your major for your whole undergraduate degree (a minor does not count). You must attend, or plan to attend, a college in the U.S. or a U.S. territory.

name: Brower Youth Awards
summary: An award for young people ages 13 to 22 who lead environmental projects in North America. Each winner gets $3,000, a short film about their work and a paid leadership trip.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application yourself and include a photo. Semifinalists are later asked for a support letter from someone who knows their environmental work (not a parent). The 2026 deadline was March 31.
amount_text: $3,000 cash prize, plus a short film and a leadership trip
deadline_text: Usually late March. The 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026.
other_requirements: You must be 13 to 22 years old on the deadline, live in North America and lead environmental work. The prize is cash, not tied to college.

name: Dr. James Earl Kennamer Scholarship Program
summary: Scholarships for graduating seniors who hunt and support wildlife conservation. Winners advance from local chapter to state to national, and the national winner receives $10,000.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the NWTF scholarship portal to one local chapter by your state's deadline. You need a 400 to 600 word essay on conservation and hunting heritage, two recommendation letters from non-relatives and a copy of your hunting license.
amount_text: Local and state awards vary; $10,000 for the national winner
deadline_text: The application opens November 1. Each state sets its own deadline, and the national winner is chosen by April 1, 2027.
other_requirements: You must be an active hunter (send a copy of your hunting license) and a current NWTF member. You also need school and community leadership. You may apply to only one chapter.

name: Ducks Unlimited National Scholarship Program
summary: Scholarships for graduating seniors who are Ducks Unlimited members and care about wetlands and waterfowl conservation. Each year there are 61 awards, from $500 up to one $10,000 national scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply online by March 1, 2027. Include a transcript, your DU member and volunteer history, your awards, up to three recommendation letters and a 500-word essay on wetlands conservation.
amount_text: 50 awards of $500, 10 of $1,000 and 1 national award of $10,000, paid to your college
deadline_text: March 1, 2027 at midnight
other_requirements: You must be a Ducks Unlimited member. Students active in DU Varsity or local DU chapters get preference.

name: GACD Scholarship
summary: A $1,000 scholarship for Georgia students with financial need who plan to study soil and water conservation or a related field. Examples include agronomy, horticulture and agricultural education.
how_to_apply: Download the application from the GACD website and submit it with your transcript by December 31, 2026.
amount_text: $1,000 (two payments of $500, one for each semester)
deadline_text: December 31, 2026
other_requirements: You must be a Georgia resident and major, or plan to major, in a soil and water conservation-related field. Past winners cannot apply again.

name: GACD Auxiliary Scholarship
sponsor: Georgia Association of Conservation Districts Auxiliary
summary: A $500 scholarship for Georgia students with financial need who plan to study a soil and water conservation-related field. The rules are the same as for the main GACD Scholarship.
how_to_apply: Download the Auxiliary application from the GACD website and send it with a current transcript by December 31, 2026.
amount_text: $500 one-time
deadline_text: December 31, 2026
other_requirements: You must be a Georgia resident and plan a soil and water conservation-related major. The money is paid after you finish one semester of full-time study.

name: Dr. Brian L. Davis Marine Biology, Conservation, and Education Scholarship
summary: A $20,000 scholarship ($5,000 a year for four years) for a public high school senior who will earn a bachelor's degree in marine biology, conservation, zoological sciences or science education.
how_to_apply: Apply online by February 15, 2027. Include an essay of up to 1,000 words (in APA style) on the biggest threats to marine biodiversity and three science-based solutions, two recommendation letters, your transcript and a resume.
amount_text: $20,000 total ($5,000 a year for four years)
deadline_text: February 15, 2027. The winner is announced April 15, 2027.
other_requirements: You must attend a public high school in the U.S. and plan a bachelor's degree in one of the listed fields at a U.S. college. Starting at a 2-year college and then transferring is allowed. Children of Georgia Aquarium employees and volunteers cannot apply. You must keep a 2.5 GPA to renew.

name: Rising Explorer Grant
summary: A research grant (about $2,000 on average) for high school and college students who plan their own field research project. Fields include biology, wildlife conservation, environmental science and marine and freshwater studies.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form with your project plan, timeline and budget, two letters of support and a short video. Applications for the 2027 field season have closed and will reopen in summer 2027.
amount_text: Awards average about $2,000
deadline_text: Closed for the 2027 field season and reopening in summer 2027. The last deadline was August 31, 2026.
other_requirements: The money pays for a field research project that creates new knowledge. Trips, adventures and school field trips do not qualify. Open to students worldwide.

name: National Ocean Scholar Program
summary: Up to $1,000 in college aid for graduating seniors who competed in the National Ocean Sciences Bowl at least once in high school and plan a career in ocean or environmental science.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (a Google Form) in the spring of senior year. The 2026 round was due May 31, 2026.
amount_text: Up to $1,000 for tuition, fees, books, a laptop or transportation
deadline_text: Late spring of senior year. The 2026 deadline was May 31, 2026.
other_requirements: You must have competed on a National Ocean Sciences Bowl team during high school (Georgia has a regional NOSB competition). The money cannot pay for room and board.

name: The Earth Prize
summary: A worldwide environmental sustainability competition for students ages 13 to 19 with more than $100,000 in prizes. Seven regional winners each get $10,000 to carry out their idea.
how_to_apply: Register on The Earth Prize website (registration runs until January 10, 2027) and submit your project by January 31, 2027.
amount_text: $10,000 for each of seven regional winners, plus $500 mentor awards
deadline_text: Register by January 10, 2027. Projects are due January 31, 2027.
other_requirements: Open to students ages 13 to 19 worldwide. The prize pays for putting a sustainability idea into action. It is not a tuition scholarship.

name: Non-Resident Merit Scholarships
summary: Merit scholarships of $2,000 to $12,000 a year for out-of-state first-year students at the College of Charleston, which has a well-known marine biology program. Every non-resident applicant is considered.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission. No separate scholarship application is needed.
deadline_text: Considered with your admission application. The page does not give a scholarship deadline.
other_requirements: For non-South Carolina residents entering as first-year students.

name: Out-of-State Freshman Merit Awards
summary: Merit awards for out-of-state freshmen at Coastal Carolina, which has a large marine science program. Awards run from $4,500 a year up to $17,988 a year for the Presidential Scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission by a priority deadline: October 15 (Early Decision), November 15 (Early Action) or February 1 (Regular Decision). You are considered automatically and told in your acceptance letter.
amount_text: $4,500 to $17,988 a year, renewable for up to 4 years
deadline_text: Priority deadlines: October 15 (Early Decision), November 15 (Early Action), February 1 (Regular Decision). Money is limited after these dates.
other_requirements: There are no set GPA or test cutoffs; the whole application is reviewed. To renew, you need a 3.0 GPA and 30 credits each year.

name: Academic Achievement Scholarships
summary: Automatic tuition scholarships of $20,000 to $28,000 a year for first-year students at Eckerd College in St. Petersburg, Florida, a school known for marine science. The amount is based on your high school GPA.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission for fall 2027. Students admitted without conditions are considered automatically.
amount_text: $20,000 to $28,000 a year for up to 4 years
deadline_text: Considered with your admission application
other_requirements: Covers tuition only.

name: Community Engagement and Leadership Scholarship
summary: A $4,000-a-year scholarship plus a $2,000 study-abroad grant for incoming Eckerd College students with strong grades and a commitment to leadership and service.
how_to_apply: Send the separate scholarship application by February 1, 2027.
amount_text: $4,000 a year plus a $2,000 study-abroad grant
deadline_text: February 1, 2027

name: First-Year Research Associateships
summary: About 25 incoming Eckerd College students get a paid spot (up to $1,000) working on research with faculty in their first year. Many Eckerd students do research in marine science.
how_to_apply: Send the separate application by February 1, 2027.
amount_text: Stipend of up to $1,000 for one year
deadline_text: February 1, 2027
other_requirements: Students are chosen based on their whole high school record.

name: UTampa Presidential Merit Scholarship
summary: A merit scholarship of $10,000 to $18,000 a year for first-year students at the University of Tampa, which offers marine science and biology majors. Every high school applicant is considered.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission. You are considered automatically, with emphasis on your unweighted GPA and how challenging your courses were.
amount_text: $10,000 to $18,000 a year, renewable for up to 8 semesters
deadline_text: Decided at admission. Awards depend on available funds, so applying early helps.
other_requirements: Leadership or community service is considered. You must stay full-time and keep making academic progress to renew. Award amounts cannot be appealed.

name: Florida Tech Merit Scholarship
summary: A merit scholarship for first-time, full-time students, both in-state and out-of-state, at Florida Tech, which offers marine biology and ocean engineering. The award is based on weighted GPA and test scores.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission. You are considered when you are admitted.
amount_text: Amount varies (not listed); renewable for up to 9 semesters
deadline_text: Considered at admission

name: Florida Tech Scouting Grant (Eagle Scout and Gold Award)
summary: $2,500 a year for incoming Florida Tech students who earned the Boy Scouts Eagle rank or the Girl Scouts Gold Award. It can be added on top of other Florida Tech scholarships.
how_to_apply: Include a copy of your Eagle Scout or Gold Award certificate with your Florida Tech admission application.
amount_text: $2,500 a year for up to 4 years
deadline_text: Submit with your admission application
other_requirements: You must have earned the Eagle Scout rank or the Girl Scout Gold Award and be a first-time, full-time student.

name: Academic Scholar Award for Nonresidents
summary: Merit packages of $6,500 to $30,000 a year for out-of-state freshmen at the University of South Carolina, which has a marine science major. Students are considered automatically.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission by December 1 to be considered. No separate scholarship application is needed.
amount_text: $6,500 to $30,000 a year ($26,000 to $120,000 over four years)
deadline_text: Apply for admission by December 1
other_requirements: Only for first-time freshmen starting in the fall. Last year's recipients averaged scores like these: SAT 1300+, ACT 28+ and a high weighted GPA for the lowest tier. These are averages, not cutoffs. To renew, you need full-time enrollment and a 3.0 GPA.

name: Top Scholar Awards (Stamps, McNair and Horseshoe Scholars)
summary: The University of South Carolina's top scholarships for out-of-state students, worth about $147,000 to $219,000 or more over four years. They include a cut to the in-state tuition rate, and Stamps and McNair add an enrichment fund.
how_to_apply: Send the university application and the South Carolina Honors College application by November 15. Finalists interview and attend Top Scholar Weekend.
amount_text: Horseshoe: $11,000 a year plus in-state tuition (over $147,000). McNair: $24,000 a year plus in-state tuition (over $199,000, plus a $14,000 enrichment fund). Stamps: about $219,000 plus a $15,000 enr
deadline_text: November 15 (Honors College application)
other_requirements: You must apply to the South Carolina Honors College. An interview and Top Scholar Weekend are required.

name: Admissions Academic Merit Scholarship (Out-of-State)
summary: Merit scholarships of $2,000 to $8,000 a year for out-of-state freshmen at the University of West Florida in Pensacola, which offers marine biology. The award is based on weighted GPA and test scores.
how_to_apply: Complete your admission file, including test scores, by December 1, 2026 for summer or fall 2027 entry. Recipients are notified in December.
deadline_text: December 1, 2026 (complete admission file)
other_requirements: Top tier: 4.0 weighted GPA and SAT 1400 or ACT 31. Some subject-area scores also count. Meeting the minimums does not guarantee an award. To renew, you need a 3.0 UWF GPA and 24 credits a year. No separate scholarship application is mentioned.

name: Out-of-State Freshman Admission Scholarship (Talent and Ability)
summary: Automatic scholarships for out-of-state freshmen at the University of South Alabama in Mobile, home to marine sciences and the Dauphin Island Sea Lab. Awards range from $2,500 a year to full tuition, and recipients also pay the in-state tuition rate.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission by the February 15 priority deadline. Admitted freshmen are reviewed automatically and notified by email.
amount_text: $2,500 a year up to full tuition, for 4 years, based on GPA and test scores, plus in-state tuition rate
deadline_text: February 15 priority admission and scholarship deadline
other_requirements: Open to U.S. citizens, permanent residents or qualified visa holders. Full tuition requires, for example, a 4.0 GPA with ACT 30 or SAT 1360, or a 3.5 GPA with ACT 32 or SAT 1420. You can send new scores in December, February or April for a possible increase.

name: Blue & Green Scholars Award and Director's Award
summary: Merit awards of $10,000 or $15,000 a year for out-of-state freshmen at Florida Gulf Coast University, which offers marine science. Students who apply early are considered automatically.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission by November 1 (Early Action is preferred). No separate scholarship application is needed.
amount_text: Scholars Award: $15,000 a year. Director's Award: $10,000 a year. Up to 4 years.
deadline_text: Apply for admission by November 1 (the date for fall 2027 entry may have passed; check with FGCU)
other_requirements: For non-Florida residents. The Scholars Award needs a 3.75 weighted GPA and SAT 1320 or ACT 28. The Director's Award needs a 3.5 weighted GPA and SAT 1200 or ACT 25. Awards are competitive and not guaranteed. To renew, you need a 3.0 GPA and 30 credits a year.

name: Out-of-State Tuition Waiver (Merit)
summary: Covers all out-of-state tuition (about $73,808 over four years) for top non-Florida freshmen at Florida State, which offers marine biology and has a coastal marine lab. It is based on coursework and test scores.
how_to_apply: Submit a complete admission application by the priority deadline to be considered automatically.
amount_text: 100% of out-of-state tuition, about $73,808 over 4 years
deadline_text: Complete your application by FSU's priority deadline (several FSU awards say to apply by December 1)
other_requirements: To renew, you need 15 credits a term and a 3.0 GPA. Some amounts on the page are labeled for students starting in fall 2024, so confirm current values.

name: President's Scholarship and Canes Achievement Award
summary: Merit scholarships for first-year students at the University of Miami, home of the Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science. They are worth up to $30,000 a year (President's) or up to $20,000 a year (Canes Achievement).
how_to_apply: Submit a complete admission application by your deadline. You are considered automatically, whatever admission plan you use.
amount_text: Up to $30,000 a year (President's) or up to $20,000 a year (Canes Achievement), for up to 8 semesters
deadline_text: Considered with your admission application
other_requirements: To keep it, you need full-time enrollment (24 credits a year) and a 3.0 GPA.

name: Premier Scholarships (Stamps, Isaac Bashevis Singer, Ronald A. Hammond, Weeks)
summary: The University of Miami's top first-year scholarships, covering full tuition or the full cost of attendance. Stamps also adds a $12,000 enrichment fund.
how_to_apply: Apply Early Decision I or Early Action by November 1. Some Premier scholarships may ask for more information.
amount_text: Full tuition (Singer, Hammond, Weeks) or full cost of attendance plus $12,000 (Stamps)
deadline_text: November 1 (Early Decision I or Early Action). For fall 2027 entry this date has passed.
other_requirements: The Hammond and Weeks scholarships are for U.S. citizens and permanent residents only.

name: George W. Jenkins Scholarship
summary: A full-cost-of-attendance scholarship plus a stipend at the University of Miami for students from eight Southeastern states, including Georgia. It looks at grades, financial need and overcoming hardship.
how_to_apply: Your school counselor must nominate you. Apply Early Decision I or Early Action by November 1.
amount_text: Full cost of attendance plus a stipend
deadline_text: November 1 (Early Decision I or Early Action). For fall 2027 entry this date has passed.
other_requirements: You must live in AL, FL, GA, KY, NC, SC, TN or VA and be nominated by your guidance counselor.

name: Non-Resident Academic Merit Scholarships (Presidential, Heritage, Charter)
summary: Merit scholarships of $7,000 to $17,000 a year for out-of-state freshmen at Auburn, which offers fisheries and aquatic sciences, wildlife and a common pre-vet path. Awards are based on GPA and ACT or SAT score.
how_to_apply: Get admitted by early February to be considered automatically. No scholarship application is needed. Send updated test scores by January 10.
deadline_text: Be admitted by early February. Updated test scores are due by January 10.
other_requirements: ACT 29-30 earns $7,000 a year, 31-32 earns $11,000, 33-34 earns $15,000 and 35-36 earns $17,000 (SAT equivalents accepted). The chart on the page is for fall 2026 entry, so amounts may change. To renew, you need a 3.0 Auburn GPA and 24 credits a year.
